workload: Identical to t25-renderer.json: 4K fixed colour buffer (3840x2160), 240x63 grid, EVERY cell rewritten every frame through Session::putChar, then split, shaped, atlased and rebuilt. Unchanged on purpose so the two compare directly.
how_to_run: cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release, then KRAIT_TERM_BENCH=<frames> KRAIT_BENCH_4K=1 KRAIT_GPU=<hardware|warp> KRAIT_BENCH_OUT=<json> krait-app.exe
preset_note: T35 added a `release` preset. Until now the release gate was measured from a hand-configured build/rel directory, which is a gate nobody else could reproduce. rules/render.md's budgets are release gates and now have a preset to match.
evidence: Every run logged 'bench: step 600, rows 63, cache hits 37643 misses 94, rowsRebuilt 63'. rowsRebuilt 63 is what proves the flood actually churned — an earlier harness reported ~2900 fps while re-drawing one static frame, and the step log exists so that can never pass silently again.

release_warp.note: Two runs: 179.9 and 180.0 fps, cpu_avg 5.557 and 5.555 — reproducible to three digits. 180.0 against a 180 Hz display means this leg is now VSYNC-BOUND, so it is a floor and not a measured ceiling: WARP is at least 180 fps, where T25 measured 139.9 and was not vsync-bound. cpu_avg includes vsync pacing for the same reason.

debug_warp.note: Debug is NOT the gate (rules/render.md: the budgets are release gates), but it is recorded so a Debug regression stays visible. T25's Debug leg was 51.3 fps on the dev GPU; this is 85.7 on WARP, and the two are not directly comparable.

release_gpu.why: NOT MEASURED this session, and deliberately not carried forward from T25 as though it were fresh. The hardware leg initialises correctly — 'render: pipelines ready (adapter NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060)', 'rhi backend: D3D11' — and then never presents a frame: synchronize() is never called, the step log stays empty, and the harness watchdog fires at 60 s. Qt also logs 'qt.qpa.screen: Unable to open monitor interface to DISPLAY1'. The machine had no usable attached display for the duration of this session, and a D3D11 present on a physical adapter with nowhere to present blocks. This is exactly the condition T26's WARP fallback exists for, so it is evidence the fallback matters rather than a renderer regression.
release_gpu.todo: Re-measure on a machine with an attached display before M2 closes; the last real number is t25-renderer.json's 140.7 fps.

gates.sixty_fps_release_flood: PASS on WARP (>=180 fps, vsync-bound). rules/render.md asks for 60 fps under cat-flood on the reference machine; the hardware leg is unmeasured this session — see release_gpu.
gates.vs_t25_warp: PASS, and by a margin: 139.9 -> at least 180 fps, cpu_avg 7.148 -> 5.555 ms. No M1 renderer change targeted this; the likeliest cause is the release preset applying optimisation flags the hand-rolled build/rel may not have carried identically. Recorded as unexplained-but-favourable rather than claimed as a win.
gates.regression_threshold: rules/render.md fails any baseline that regresses more than 5%. For M2, compare release_warp: cpu_avg_ms must stay at or under 5.83, and rowsRebuilt must stay 63.
